name: Electrically Power-Assisted Cycle
description: Queensland's e-bike since 1 July 2026: a pedal cycle that complies with the EN 15194 edition in force when it was made and carries a permanent compliance label, so no more than 250 W, assisting only to 25 km/h and on a throttle only to 6 km/h; older and adaptive e-bikes can be verified and labelled instead. Riders must be 16 and hold a driver licence, and are held to 12 km/h on footpaths.

restrictions.rule: Two or more wheels, built to be propelled by human power through a belt, chain or gears, with one or more auxiliary electric motors
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), sch. 4 (definition of electrically power-assisted cycle)

restrictions.rule: Complies with EN 15194 as in force when it was manufactured, and has a label permanently attached indicating that it does
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), sch. 4 (definitions of electrically power-assisted cycle and EPAC standard); Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Road Rules) Regulation 2009 (Qld), s. 353B

restrictions.rule: No more than 250 W continuous rated power, motor assistance only while pedalling and only to 25 km/h, and a throttle only up to 6 km/h to help start moving

Alternatively, a legacy EPAC verified and labelled under the assurance scheme: made before 1 July 2026, with pedals, no more than 250 W continuous rated power, no faster than 6 km/h on the motor alone, assistance cut off at 25 km/h, and no feature that bypasses those limits
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 122Q; Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Accreditation and Other Provisions) Regulation 2015 (Qld), s. 129D

restrictions.rule: Or a special purpose EPAC, designed or modified for a rider with a disability or medical condition and verified and labelled: pedals, no faster than 12 km/h on the motor alone, and assistance cut off at 25 km/h; or a vehicle under a special circumstances permit
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 122Q, sch. 4; Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Accreditation and Other Provisions) Regulation 2015 (Qld), s. 129E

restrictions.rule: One made before 1 July 2026 that met Queensland's former power-assisted bicycle definition counts as one without a label until 28 February 2027
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 245; Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Accreditation and Other Provisions) Regulation 2015 (Qld), s. 177

restrictions.rule: A rider must be at least 16 and hold a driver licence, a learner licence at minimum, to ride on a road, road-related area or public place
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 78B(1)

restrictions.rule: Except a child of at least 12 riding under close adult supervision, a licence-ineligible rider of 16 or older with a medical exemption certificate, or anyone riding on a mountain bike trail, rail trail or private recreational cycling facility
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Accreditation and Other Provisions) Regulation 2015 (Qld), ss. 129A–129C

restrictions.rule: No faster than 12 km/h crossing a road at a crossing or on an unsigned footpath, the signed limit on a signed path, and 12 km/h passing a pedestrian on a shared path
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management—Road Rules) Regulation 2009 (Qld), ss. 24D, 250A

restrictions.rule: One resembling an e-bike that doesn't meet the definition is a prohibited bike, which police can seize, impound and destroy
restrictions.citation: Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 (Qld), s. 6
